D018-D011_h001.question_both:
I'm not exactly sure why I'm here. My husband, Mark, thinks I've been a bit off since ... a few months ago. It's hard to put a finger on it. I’ve been having these terrible dreams, some nights, it feels like I’m right back there, the fear is so real. I used to love our weekend hikes, but now, I just can't seem to get excited about anything.

Honestly, it feels like everyone around me just moved on. It’s like they don’t understand how much *that day* really changed things. If only certain people had been more careful, none of this would have happened. And the shock... sometimes it feels like it just happened yesterday. Then there are other days when I just can't make a decision – even picking out an outfit for a shoot feels impossible. And if someone touches me unexpectedly, even Mark, I just jump out of my skin. It’s all just so overwhelming.
D018-D011_h001.question_a:
Lately, it feels like I’m living in a fog. Every night, the same dream replays—the accident, the shattered glass, and the screams. It’s been five months since it happened, and I still wake up in a cold sweat, the horror of it all just as fresh as if it were yesterday. My husband says I’ve changed. I used to love finding new places for shoots and experimenting with lighting, but now, the thought of picking up my camera just feels… heavy. I’ve lost all interest in my photography, which was my entire world.

I know it sounds irrational, but I can't shake the feeling that the other driver, the one who caused the pile-up, got off too easy. I constantly find myself replaying the scene and blaming him for every little thing that’s gone wrong since. Even simple things, like choosing what to wear in the morning or what to have for dinner, have become agonizing decisions. I just freeze up. And don't even get me started on being touched unexpectedly. If someone brushes past me, even an accident, I jump out of my skin – it’s like I’m always on edge. This constant state of anxiety, this jumpiness, and feeling so detached, it all just circles back to that day on the highway.
D018-D011_h001.question_b: Lately, it feels like I’m constantly on edge, and it’s been going on for months now. I just can’t relax, and honestly, this constant worry isn't tied to any one thing. The joy I used to get from photography, seeing happy couples, it’s just not there anymore. It’s hard to even pick out an outfit in the morning, let alone make decisions for my business. I’m also having these awful dreams, reliving moments of a car accident I was in a few years ago. I still feel the shock and terror of that crash, like it happened yesterday. And if someone touches me unexpectedly, even my husband, I jump out of my skin. It’s exhausting.

I just feel… off.

Now, I feel a lot like a stranger in my own life. Sometimes, I’ll be doing something totally normal, like putting away tools, and suddenly I’m right back there on the factory floor, seeing it all happen again, feeling the heat, hearing the screams, even though I'm clearly in my garage. It’s like a movie playing in my head, and I can't stop it.

I used to enjoy tinkering in the garage, spending time with my wife, but all that joy is gone. Nothing gives me that old spark. I keep replaying that day, thinking about what I could have done differently. If I’d just checked that valve one more time, maybe it wouldn't have happened. The shame… it’s a constant weight. I try to avoid anything that reminds me of it, which is half of everything these days. My patience is shot too. I’m constantly on edge, the slightest unexpected movement from my wife or even a shadow out of the corner of my eye makes me jump out of my skin. And my memory's going, too. I forget where I put my keys or even what I needed to do next. It's like my mind is so preoccupied with avoiding thoughts of the accident and the anxiety it brings, that there's no room for anything else. The constant anxiety and being so irritable, it’s all tied back to that day.
